news.title: One month after World Cup final, Argentine Football Association president explodes against conspiracists
news.lede: One month ago, Spain won the World Cup final against Argentina, and a series of conspiracy teories, some implying that they had lost on purpose for a variety or reasons, like threats by FIFA, secret deals or anything but to accept that they had not been better than their rivals. Today, Claudio "Chiqui" Tapia, President of the Argentine Football Association, has written a strongly worded statement slamming all of those who started those conspiracy theories and of course were never proved." A month since that final. A month since the lies, the manipulation, and a despicable campaign to portray this team as having thrown the game.

news.title: Messi retirement hint highlights football era nearing an end
news.lede: Soon after propelling Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup final, Lionel Messi has cast some doubt on his future. While retirement doesn't seem imminent, it still beckons for him and Cristiano Ronaldo. "I'm really not sure if I'll carry on doing it for much longer." Those words earlier this month from Lionel Messi, a man who famously says very little, sparked a global conversation about whether his storied career was about to end.

news.title: Olopade Calls for Calm After Historic World Cup Failure, Shifts Focus to Other Sports
news.lede: Director General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Bukola Olopade, has called for calm following the Super Falcons’ failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, insisting that defeat is an unavoidable part of competitive sport. Nigeria’s hopes of reaching the tournament in Brazil were ended after the Super Falcons suffered a 2–1 defeat to South Africa in the decisive World Cup play-off in Casablanca. The result ended Nigeria’s remarkable record of qualifying for every edition of the Women’s World Cup since the competition began in 1991.

news.title: ‘World Cup Failure Shouldn’t Erase the Progress’ — Hassan Wada Defends NFF Record
news.lede: Chairman of the Kogi State Football Association, Hassan Wada, has defended the Nigeria Football Federation against growing criticism following the country’s failure to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup and the 2027 Women’s World Cup. Wada argued that the NFF’s performance should be assessed across a broader period rather than being judged solely on World Cup qualification. The Kogi FA chairman pointed to Nigeria’s recent performances at the Africa Cup of Nations, highlighting the Super Eagles’ second-place finish at the 2023 AFCON and third-place finish at the 2025 edition.

news.title: 'Incredible Experience': World Cup Winner Paul Pogba Released By Monaco
news.lede: Former Manchester United and Juventus midfielder Paul Pogba has been released by Monaco after a single season, in a move that could spell the end of his career in Europe. Pogba, 33, won the World Cup with France in 2018 but since serving a ban for doping has struggled to return to the elite level and has been plagued by injuries. Monaco said in a statement that the objectives they had set were “only partially achieved” and the Ligue 1 club were therefore terminating his contract that would have run until June 2027. Pogba is currently sidelined with a thigh injury, just after returning from a knee problem.

news.title: Nigerians drive SuperSport’s 19 billion World Cup digital views
news.lede: Spain's midfielder #16 Rodri lifts the trophy with his teammates after winning the 2026 World Cup football tournament final match between Spain and Argentina at the New York/New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford on July 19, 2026. Nigerian football fans were among the biggest participants in SuperSport’s digital FIFA World Cup 2026 experience, accounting for 21.2 per cent of users of the SuperSport Predictor, the broadcaster has announced. Post-tournament figures released by SuperSport showed that Nigerian users were second only to South Africans, who accounted for 29.5 per cent of registered users on the Predictor platform on Tuesday. The tournament, which was played in the USA, Canada and Mexico from June 11 to July 19, ended with Spain beating Argentina 1-0 in the final in New Jersey.

news.title: Brazilian football legend reportedly converts to Islam after marrying Moroccan woman
news.lede: Dubai: News coming out of Turkey has reported that Brazilian football legend Roberto Carlos has converted to Islam.. Reports from several Turkish newspapers, claim that 53-year-old converted to Islam around four weeks ago after reciting the Shahada during a meeting with Sheikh Jihad Hamada, a prominent figure in Brazil’s Muslim community.. However, the claims are yet to be confirmed by the former Real Madrid defender.. The reports emerged after Ali Sahin, a Turkish lawmaker said he had learned about Carlos’ alleged conversion from a prominent member of Brazil’s Muslim community..
